title: Best Time of Year for Air Duct Cleaning
h1: What Is the Best Time of Year for Air Duct Cleaning?
description: Spring and fall are usually the best times for air duct cleaning in Southern California. Learn why, plus the events that mean you should not wait.
quick_answer: Spring and fall are usually the best times for air duct cleaning in Southern California. The weather is mild, you can go without heating or cooling for a few hours, and you start the busy season with clean ducts. Some events, like a remodel, a rodent problem or heavy wildfire smoke, are reasons to clean right away regardless of season.
body:
Why are spring and fall the best seasons?

Duct cleaning means shutting the system off for a few hours while the ducts are opened up and cleaned under negative pressure. In spring and fall that's easy. Nobody is sweating through an inland heat wave or shivering on a cold January night while the work gets done.

Timing it before the heavy-use season also makes sense. Clean ducts in spring means the AC moves clean air all summer. Clean ducts in fall means the first furnace run of the year doesn't push a season's worth of dust into the house.

Is spring or fall better?

Either works. A few things might tip it one way:

  • Spring makes sense if allergies flare when pollen comes in, or if you run the AC a lot in summer, as many inland homes do.
  • Fall makes sense after a dusty summer, after wildfire season or Santa Ana winds have pushed smoke and grit into the house, or before the furnace starts running.
  • Pair it with a tune-up. Many homeowners clean ducts around the same time as their seasonal HVAC maintenance, so the whole system is clean at once.

When should you clean ducts no matter the season?

Some situations don't wait for a nice season:

  1. After a remodel. Drywall dust and sawdust get pulled into returns even when you're careful. Clean once the dusty work is done.
  2. After rodents or pests. Droppings or nesting in ducts should be cleaned out, and the ducts sanitized.
  3. After significant smoke exposure. Wildfire smoke or a house fire can leave soot and odor in the ductwork.
  4. When you see mold. Visible growth on duct surfaces or around the coil needs attention, along with the moisture problem that caused it.
  5. When moving into a home. You don't know the history. A cleaning gives you a fresh start.
  6. When vents puff dust. If you see dust blow out when the system starts, the ducts are loaded.

What happens during a duct cleaning visit?

Knowing what's involved helps you pick a day. A typical visit looks like this:

  1. The technician inspects the system, including the registers, returns and accessible ducts in the attic.
  2. A negative-pressure collection unit is connected to the duct system so loosened debris is pulled out, not blown into the house.
  3. Each supply and return is agitated with brushes or air whips to free buildup.
  4. Registers and grilles are cleaned, and the filter is replaced.
  5. If needed, the system is sanitized and any obvious leaks or disconnected ducts are noted for repair.

Plan to have someone home and the system off for the duration.

How often should air ducts be cleaned?

There's no fixed calendar rule that fits every house. Many homes go several years between cleanings. You'll want to clean more often if you have pets, allergy or asthma sufferers, smokers, frequent remodeling, or a home that sees a lot of dust from nearby construction or dry inland winds.

Coastal and inland homes can differ too. Homes near busy roads, canyons or open land inland often collect more fine dust, especially after Santa Ana wind events, while coastal homes tend to see more moisture-related buildup around the coil and supply registers.

Your filter is a good clue. If it loads up fast or you see dust around the edges of supply registers, the system is moving more debris than it should.

What should you do after duct cleaning?

A cleaning works best when you keep the ducts from getting dirty again:

  • Put in a fresh, good-quality filter and change it on schedule.
  • Make sure the filter fits snugly with no gaps around it.
  • Ask about sealing leaky return ducts, which pull in attic or garage dust.
  • Keep supply and return grilles clear and wipe them down now and then.

Our air duct cleaning service uses negative-pressure equipment to clean the whole system, not just the vents you can reach. Spring and fall fill up, so check current specials and book early.
faqs: Can air ducts be cleaned in summer?

Yes. The system is off for a few hours during the cleaning, so on a very hot day the house may warm up. Booking for the morning helps. If you need it done because of smoke, rodents or a remodel, the season matters much less than getting it handled.
How long does air duct cleaning take?

Most homes take a few hours, depending on size, number of vents and how much debris is in the system. Larger homes or homes with multiple systems take longer. Your technician can give a time estimate after seeing the layout.
Does duct cleaning help with allergies?

It can help if the ducts are actually dirty, because the system will stop recirculating that debris. For lasting results, pair it with a better filter and sealing any leaky return ducts, so dust from the attic or garage stops getting pulled in.
